name: Green Chilli
botanical: Capsicum annuum L. (also C. frutescens, C. chinense)
perishability: Highly perishable. 3–5 days before shrivelling or turning red.
summary: Bought in small amounts but in every kitchen, so it is a sensitive item in household budgets. It is picked many times over several months from scattered belts, cannot be stored, and swings sharply with heat and rain. India is also the world's largest producer and exporter of dry red chilli, a separate market.

key_numbers.label: Dry chilli
key_numbers.note: largest producer and exporter of dry red chilli (separate market)

global: India leads world chilli production. Fresh green chilli exports go mainly to the UAE, UK, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Nepal.

states.basis: Leading green-chilli states (ranked; shares not shown because published figures vary widely)

belts.name: Nimar
belts.note: Large green and dry chilli belt supplying North India.

belts.name: North Karnataka
belts.note: Green chilli plus Byadgi dry chilli (GI).

belts.name: Guntur–Khammam
belts.note: Mainly dry chilli, also green for southern cities.

belts.name: Nandurbar
belts.note: Large green chilli market for Mumbai and Gujarat.

belts.name: North-East
belts.note: Bhut jolokia, Naga mircha and bird's-eye chilli (GI).

seasons.name: Kharif
seasons.note: Main crop; pickings run into winter.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.note: Heat stress; supplies the early monsoon months.

lean_season: June–August, when summer pickings end and kharif has not started.

climate.v: 20–30 °C ideal. Flowers drop above ~35 °C and below ~15 °C.
600–1,250 mm; heavy rain at flowering causes flower drop and fruit rot.
Well-drained loam, pH 6.5–7.5. Cannot stand waterlogging.
Hot, dry weather raises capsaicin; variety still matters most.

weather_risks.impact: Flower and fruit drop; summer crop shrinks.
weather_risks.example: 2024 summer heat pushed retail prices up in June.

weather_risks.impact: Flower drop, anthracnose and die-back; transplanting delays.
Slow growth and poor fruit set.

pests.name: Thrips and mites (leaf-curl complex, 'murda')
pests.impact: Leaf curl and stunting; major yield loss.

pests.name: Invasive black thrips
pests.impact: Devastated AP, Telangana and Karnataka chilli in 2021-22.

postharvest.chilling: Chilling injury below ~7 °C: pitting and soft spots.
practices: Picked green and firm, often early morning; sorted to remove reddening fruit.
Packed in jute or leno bags (20–40 kg); some long-distance loads iced in summer.
Shrivelling (water loss) is the main defect; shade and fast transit matter.

steps.what: Repeated pickings; small farmers bring bags to the nearest APMC.
Auction at Nandurbar, Khargone, Belagavi, Guntur and similar markets.
Overnight trucks (sometimes rail parcels) to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad.
Sold by 100–250 g; often bundled free with vegetables by vendors.

supply_chain.packaging: Jute or leno bags; open trucks.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Arka Lohit, Arka Meghana, Arka Harita
Bajji / bhavnagari chilli
varieties.note: Large mild type for fritters and stuffing.

varieties.name: Bhut jolokia, Naga mircha, Mizo bird's-eye

trade.exports: Fresh green chilli: modest, to the Gulf, UK and Nepal. Dry chilli: India is the largest exporter (China, Bangladesh, Thailand, Sri Lanka).

policy.what: No MSP or buffer. Spices Board covers dry chilli only.

history.what: Retail often ₹100–200/kg as summer pickings end.
Thrips parvispinus outbreak cut southern chilli output sharply.
Winter glut; farm prices fall to ₹5–15/kg.

signals: Arrivals in Nandurbar, Khargone and Hyderabad markets (Agmarknet).
Max temperature anomalies in May–June in central India.
Pest advisories (thrips) from state universities in the South.
business: Small ticket, high frequency: a staple add-on item for quick commerce baskets, so availability matters more than margin.
Very high price per kg at retail (₹100+/kg in small packs) versus ₹20–50/kg at wholesale for much of the year.
Cold chain at 7–10 °C roughly triples saleable life; most of the trade still runs without it.
